extracted.intended_audience: candidates, sponsors, and peer reviewers of NIH fellowship applications (due on or after January 25, 2025)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for NIH fellowship (individual NRSA-style) applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2025, focusing reviewer attention and reducing bias in selection of early-career trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship candidate's preparedness and potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Better focus reviewer attention on the fellowship candidate's preparedness and potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of three key assessments the revised review criteria emphasize. Reviewers should evaluate the candidate's current capabilities, trajectory, prior accomplishments, and likelihood to succeed and benefit from the proposed fellowship training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research training plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Better focus reviewer attention on the research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the quality, appropriateness, and feasibility of the proposed research training (mentorship, training activities, timeline, and how the plan advances the candidate's development). This is explicitly highlighted as a primary review dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to the candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Better focus reviewer attention on the commitment to the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the sponsor's and institution's demonstrated commitment to supporting the candidate (e.g., mentorship, resources, protected time). The revised criteria emphasize assessing commitment as separate from institutional or sponsor prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and simplicity of application and review language
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure a broad range of candidates and research training contexts can be recognized as meritorious by clarifying and simplifying the language in the application and review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and review instructions are to be written more plainly so diverse training environments and nontraditional candidate backgrounds are not disadvantaged by opaque or overly technical wording. This supports equitable recognition of merit across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce bias by de-emphasizing sponsor/institution reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce bias in review by emphasizing the commitment to the candidate without undue consideration of sponsor and institutional reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are instructed to avoid letting sponsor or institutional prestige unduly influence judgments. The revised criteria explicitly prioritize direct evidence of candidate potential and sponsor commitment over reputational signals.
